rows.39:c234:
It's obvious, isn't it?
Yoko had a younger twin sister who was adopted out to a relative's family when they were small.
Apparently Yoko wasn't very healthy when she was little.
That's supposedly why she and her sister ended up living apart.
The two of them knew about each other, and I hear they kept in touch a lot.
Though they hardly ever got to see each other...{p}
rows.39:d158:
"I see...
So you can tell after all."
Fukuzawa murmured, and a slightly lonely look came into her eyes.
"Then I'll tell you a little about that ghost."
Did Fukuzawa know something about that ghost, {f:I wondered|I wondered}?
"This was a long, long time ago, back when the old school building was still in use.
There was a girl who killed herself because she was being bullied.
Nobody would have anything to do with her, and it hurt so much to have her very existence ignored that she hanged herself on that staircase...
She thought that if she did, everyone would surely look at her.
But not a single person cried for her.
Everyone forgot about her right away."
Fukuzawa was speaking slowly, as if choosing her words.
Her voice wasn't loud, but in the hushed room it had a strange weight to it.
"And so, the girl who died couldn't leave that staircase.
But nobody would look at her, just like when she was alive...
So she was lonely..."{p}
rows.39:d900:
"Hee hee hee, sorry.
I was lying to you.
The story about the thirteen steps in the old school building was a lie.
I don't have any friends who'd hang around with me."
"But why★
Was the whole story a lie{f:, then|, then}?"
"Not all of it.
The story about the girl who killed herself is true.
Because that girl is me!"{p}
rows.39:dd48:
Well, they do say there are three people in the world who look just like you.
Hmm, I guess you could say that, but I see it a little differently.
I've heard of doppelgangers too, and usually it's your own double that you see.
They say if you see your own doppelganger you die soon after, but that isn't always the case.
The most famous one is probably the story about a European poet.
You see, back when he had no position or fame yet, he left his village, promising his sweetheart that he'd come back for her without fail.
At that moment, on the road in front of her house, he saw a fine young man on horseback coming from the opposite direction.
They say the rider was dressed in blue.
Then, a few years later.
The poet made it big in the city and went to fetch his sweetheart, just as he'd promised.
He was now riding back on horseback along the road he'd once walked.
The thought made his heart skip a beat.
Right now, he was wearing blue and riding a horse.
Just like the young man he'd passed long ago...
The one he'd seen back then had been his other self.
This poet went on to live for decades after that.
So seeing a doppelganger doesn't mean you'll die right away.
Though in this poet's case, you could also say time had crossed over.
So then, why do people say you'll die soon if you see your doppelganger...?
It's because a lot of people really do die, right?
And as for why they die...
Hmm, what I'm about to tell you is pretty far-fetched. Is that okay?
Then again, if I don't tell you this, the story won't end.
Oh well, if you can't believe it, just let it go in one ear and out the other.{p}
rows.39:e2bc:
Do you believe in reincarnation and that sort of thing?
I do. Being reborn, I mean.
Most of the time, one life is reborn as one life, but they say once in a while a soul splits apart when it's reborn.
For example, let's say you and I, {c}{f:|}, were one single person in a past life.
Now the two of us have met here, so this state is what they call a doppelganger.
They say people who share the same soul look alike and give off a similar air.
That's why you end up thinking, 'There's another me.'
The reason it's tied to death is that the split soul tries to become one again.
And when that happens, the one who survives is usually the person holding the biggest fragment of the split soul.
Apparently sometimes they all die, though.
And even if they never meet, they say they can't live very long.
They're incomplete somehow, I guess.
Oh, and another example people give of a doppelganger is the astral body.
It means leaving your body, and I think it happens a lot to people who work themselves too hard.
When their body's already at its limit but they just can't take a rest... at times like that, the astral body alone slips out of the flesh and lies sleeping in their room, and so on.
Other people can see it too, so there are cases where you get a phone call from someone who's sleeping right in front of you, both of them turn out to be the real person, and everyone panics...
In that case too, they say most people die once they see their other self.{p}
rows.39:e924:
They say neither of them can live long while the soul stays split, so maybe it turned out for the best.
Hee hee hee, so how was my story?
Looks like your head's all jumbled up.
But I don't want to talk about it anymore.
I'm about to get confused myself.
Come on, let's hurry on to the next one.{p}
rows.39:ea14:
Hee hee, I knew it.
Mr. Miyama suddenly felt ashamed of how he'd been acting, too.
Once he calmed down and thought it over rationally, he regretted that ever since he'd confiscated the ring, he'd behaved in a way no adult ever should.
And what came back to him was the man he'd been when he'd had nothing but pure feelings for Ishikawa.
Why hadn't he treated her with the feelings he'd had back then?
He'd been treating a girl in the middle of adolescence the wrong way.
...He wasn't a bad teacher at heart, I guess.
The teacher decided this confession should be made to Ishikawa herself, so he took that ruby ring and headed for her house.{p}
rows.39:f848:
Hee hee hee, nobody can ever know the real truth, right?
That's where my story ends.
I'll tell you the thirteen-steps story another day, so go and see it for yourself first.
Then I'll tell you all about it.
Who's next...?{p}
